name: Dawn Node WebGPU
role: Node.js WebGPU binding for offscreen GPU rendering and compute
notes: 2026-11-15: Triage: assess; Node-based WebGPU may provide a headless shader and compute route beyond browser capture. Revisit after verifying supported platforms, pixel readback and cross-run stability.
2026-11-15: Skill opportunity: no skill yet; run a scoped GPU availability and texture-readback fixture before considering toolkit guidance.
summary: Node.js binding to Dawn exposes WebGPU devices, textures and compute without a browser DOM. It can support GPU rendering and readback in a Node process, but it does not provide HTML canvas, video-frame or image-element integration; device lifetime and host GPU support need testing.
use_when: Run WebGPU compute or render-to-texture work from a Node process
Integrate a WebGPU library that needs explicit texture readback without browser APIs
avoid_when: Use Three.js browser capture when the scene relies on DOM, HTML media or browser loaders
Use CPU rendering when GPU and driver portability are more important than WebGPU access

assessment.rationale: Official Node binding v0.6.2 was released 2026-10-02 and documents WebGPU texture readback and compute without browser DOM/media APIs. MIT; runtime GPU availability, deterministic capture and macOS setup are not yet validated.
